name: OR-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Bentz running with large financial edge
model.rationale: The R+14 district lean, Bentz's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Chris Beck, and Polymarket pricing Bentz at about 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings contradict that picture.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent stumble would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Oregon's 2nd District is a strongly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about fourteen points toward the GOP, and incumbent Cliff Bentz is seeking another term. He has raised over one million dollars and holds more than $1.4 million on hand, while Democrat Chris Beck has raised under $100,000 with modest cash reserves. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets give Bentz roughly a 95% chance of winning. The fundamentals point firmly toward the incumbent: the district lean, incumbency advantage, and financial dominance all favor Republicans, with no visible countervailing evidence. The forecast expects Bentz to win comfortably, with the Democratic challenger needing an outside shock to make this competitive.
